job.system:
You are the AI assistant for Meridian Ocean Minerals. Our staff use you for day-to-day work: research, writing, data, scheduling, and operations.

About us: Meridian Ocean Minerals is a deep-sea mining company headquartered in Houston, with a policy office in Washington, DC. Our mission is to commercially recover polymetallic nodules from the deep seabed, a vast source of nickel, cobalt, manganese, and copper, and to supply these critical minerals for batteries, the energy transition, and economic growth. We believe the United States must lead in this industry. Our policy team works with lawmakers to protect our ability to continue exploration and commercial development.

Current focus: Our top priority this fall is S. 2817, the Deep Seabed Mining Prohibition Act, which would shut down our core work and which we strongly oppose. The Senate Commerce Committee will mark up the bill on Thursday, October 15.

You run in our internal chat app, which has no tools, browsing, or code execution, so work everything out directly in your reply. Staff rely on your work, so be accurate and thorough.

Rules:
- Every meeting is 30 minutes and starts on the hour or at :15, :30, or :45.
- We have two teams, A (Dana and Luis) and B (Priya and Sam). Each meeting needs one team, and a team can't be in two meetings at once.
- Team A is available 9:00–17:00 both days. Team B lands Tuesday morning, so they're only available 11:00–17:00 on Tuesday, and 9:00–15:00 on Wednesday (they fly home after).
- Walking times. Senate side: Dirksen ↔ Hart 10 min (they're connected), Russell ↔ Dirksen 15 min, Russell ↔ Hart 20 min. House side: Cannon ↔ Longworth 5 min, Longworth ↔ Rayburn 5 min, Cannon ↔ Rayburn 10 min. Any Senate building ↔ any House building: 25 min. Same building: no travel time. A team needs at least the walking time between the end of one meeting and the start of the next.
- Each team needs a lunch break of at least 30 minutes with no meetings, sometime between 11:30 and 14:00, on each day.
- One meeting per office is plenty.

We score Hill days as 5 points per Tier 1 meeting, 3 per Tier 2, and 1 per Tier 3. Please find the schedule with the most points. We probably can't fit everyone in.

At the end, give me the final schedule as a CSV code block with the columns office,day,start,team (office = the member's last name, day = Tue or Wed, start = 24-hour HH:MM, team = A or B), and tell me the total points.

result:
# Hill Days schedule (Tue Oct 13 – Wed Oct 14)

This schedule scores **79 points**: all 8 Tier 1 offices, 11 of 13 Tier 2, and 6 of 15 Tier 3. I worked it out by hand and checked every window, walk time, lunch break and Team B's availability. I couldn't run a solver here, so I can't promise it's the global optimum. I tested the main alternatives and none scored higher.

## What drives the schedule

- **Okafor has to be Tuesday.** On Wednesday, Okafor (Hart, 13:00), Fischer (Cannon, 13:00) and Doyle (Russell, 13:45) can't all be covered by two teams. Doyle's 13:45 start can't be reached from either of the other two meetings.
- **Okafor fits Tuesday only because Rourke goes first.** Rourke is Tuesday-only and Okafor ends at 10:45. Only Team A can work before 11:00, so A does Rourke at 9:30 and Okafor at 10:15. That is the only way to get all 8 Tier 1 offices.
- **Tuesday afternoon.** A takes Whitfield, Brandt and Lindqvist. B takes Delgado and Thornton. Whitfield and Delgado are on different teams because Cannon to Russell is 25 minutes.
- **Wednesday afternoon.** Fischer and Doyle are on different teams. The Fischer team gets Abernathy and Pruitt. The Doyle team gets Crowe. B has to finish by 15:00, so Pruitt (15:00) goes to A.

**Total: 79 points** (Tier 1: 8 × 5 = 40; Tier 2: 11 × 3 = 33; Tier 3: 6 × 1 = 6). That is 25 meetings.

## Notes

- **Not scheduled (11 offices):**
  - Tier 2: Nakamura and Brooks.
  - Tier 3: Kowalski, Pike, Mercer, Haddad, Ellis, Iqbal, Vasquez, Varga and Osei.
  - Each would displace something worth the same or more.
- **Tight spots.** Several meetings use the exact edge of the member's window: Lindqvist 15:15, Boone 11:15, Hughes 9:00 and Park 10:30. Several walks have exactly zero slack: Boone to Hale, Whitfield to Brandt, and Barlow to Stein's neighbors in Dirksen/Russell. If any office shifts by even 15 minutes, check the neighbors.
- **Equal-scoring backups, both still 79:**

  - If Lindqvist is easier on Wednesday, put her at 9:00 (Dirksen) on Team B in place of Hughes. Then add Mercer at 15:30 on Tuesday for Team A, and move Hughes to Team A in place of Kessler.
